three_way_isolation.reading: SAME endpoints, SAME parameters, SAME kernel, SAME patch chain, SAME guide: it succeeds alone and fails in the full run => the difference is the ORDER: earlier edges have already been routed.

root_cause_code_site: tools/k2_p4_mroute_v1.py:771-780: after every successful solve the maze APPENDS the newly added copper back into ctx (ctx.tracks.append(...) / ctx.vias[...] = ... / ctx.holes.append(...)), so every later edge sees it as an obstacle. The last-served net is therefore starved by copper that did not exist when the run started - the classic winner-takes-all order effect, registered as M-ENG-BLOCK-CONTENTION-NEGOTIATION.
consequence: I2C2_SCL is NOT a start-side, domain or drawing problem: it is a CONTENTION problem. The remedy is the means already registered for it - rip-up-and-reroute / negotiated congestion (pass 2): when an edge fails, rip the copper that sealed it (or re-solve the suite with a congestion cost) and try again, bounded.

landed_this_window.A: the last hard domain is GONE from the chain: no --channels is emitted any more; the legacy whole-net bands are merged into --guide as @band preferences (n_nets=18 -> n_guide=66, source=hard-DROPPED(merged-into-guide)). A fail-closed gate refuses to use a rect that cannot contain an edge's endpoints as a domain (loud, recorded in the precheck as channel_domain_refused) and demotes it to guidance. HONEST LIMIT: containment is necessary but NOT sufficient - the real starvation here happened INSIDE a containing band, so the gate is a safety net, and the substantive protection is that the chain now emits no hard domain at all.
